title: Scale policy chaos testplan — failure-mode catalog and metric thresholds
sheet_data:
PURPOSE:
Catalog and test plan for intentional 'chaos' inputs to the autoscaler to find brittle failure modes and validate mitigations. This is a hands-on spreadsheet-style runbook to exercise min/max boundaries, trigger hysteresis, probe lag, and partial node failures across regions.

SCOPE:
- Focus on GPU-backed serving pools only (A100/H100-like).
- Regions: us-west1, us-east1, europe-west1, ap-south1 (selected noisy region).
- Policies: min/max (min fixed 4, min varied), scale-up trigger (queued_requests_per_gpu), scale-down trigger (idle_seconds), probe interval and probe-timeout fuzzing.

KEY DEFINITIONS AND HYPOTHESES:
- Probe-fuzzing: random delays or dropped responses from health probes to emulate network jitter. Hypothesis: short probe jitter causes spurious scale-downs if not squelched.
- Grace-window amplifier: temporarily decrease scale-down sensitivity to validate graceful recovery. Hypothesis: amplifying grace window reduces oscillation but increases coldstart risk.
- Out-of-order metrics: simulate telemetry lag where short-lived surges arrive late. Hypothesis: naive rolling-window triggers cause over scale-up.

TEST MATRIX (rows are canonical test-cases we run per-region):

CASE	DESCRIPTION	REGION	INIT_MIN	INIT_MAX	LOAD_PROFILE	TRIGGER_MODIFICATIONS	EXPECTED_BEHAVIOR	SUCCESS_CRITERIA	NOTES
1	Probe jitter (5-30s)	us-west1	4	120	steady 65% util + 30s jitter	probe-interval=10s->random 5-30s	No sustained scale-downs during transient probe failures; no >3% request drops	coldstart rate <0.5% over 60m, p95 latency within +25%	Run 3x rolling windows, capture probe logs
2	Burst then vanish (surge 10x for 90s)	us-east1	6	200	10s spike every 15m	scale-up aggressiveness +20%	Scaler must add capacity within SLA (90s) then scale down no faster than grace-window	Scale-up time <=90s; scale-down not before 8m after last peak	Record token cost delta
3	Telemetry lag (2m delayed metrics)	europe-west1	5	150	intermittent spikes, metrics delayed	rolling-window 1m->3m (simulated delay)	No over-provisioning >40% idle retention after spike; prefer conservative scale-up	Idle gpu fraction <30% after 10m; no oscillation cycles	Compare with time-series backfills
4	Partial node failure (25% GPUs on node lost)	ap-south1	8	160	steady 75% then node loss at t=12m	scale-down disabled for 10m after loss	Autoscaler should recognize reduced capacity and avoid double-scaling decisions	Requests dropped <2%, recovery time <6m	Introduce 1 simulated node OTA failure
5	Min edge-case (min set to 0->1 transition)	us-west1	0->1	100	gentle rising traffic	min-breach detection enabled	Ensure pool never goes to zero for critical routes; fallback to reserve pool if min==0	No mid-window request rejections; fallback invoked if min==0 and load>threshold	This is a canary path for reserved capacity policy
6	Oscillation chase (rapid alternating 3m high/low)	us-east1	4	120	3m on/off cycles	hysteresis reduced to 30s	Should not oscillate more than 2 full cycles before dampening; hysteresis prevents thrash	Oscillation cycles <=2 in 30m; token cost delta tracked	Compare baseline hysteresis 120s vs tuned 300s

EXPERIMENT LOG (summary entries from preliminary runs):
- 2026-06-03 us-west1 CASE1: probe jitter 5-30s. Result: scaler triggered 4 spurious scale-down events in 4h window. Root cause: probe timeout interpreted as zero healthy GPUs causing immediate scale-down. Mitigation: introduce probe-squelch (require 2 consecutive probe failures) + increase probe timeout from 5s->12s.
- 2026-06-04 us-east1 CASE2: 90s spikes. Result: scale-up latency 110s median (missed SLA). Cause: batching manager throttled new worker launches. Mitigation: pre-warm policy for scheduled spikes, pre-warm token pool allocated.
- 2026-06-05 europe-west1 CASE3: 2m telemetry lag. Result: observed over-provisioning artifact when delayed metrics arrived post-spike (idle fraction +52%). Mitigation: apply weighted decay to metric windows, prefer conservative scale-up, and attach detection for late-arriving maxima.
- 2026-06-06 ap-south1 CASE4: partial node failure. Result: transient request queuing increased p95 by 40% for 3m. Autoscaler attempted scale-up but hit regional quota; fallback policy served from adjacent region. Mitigation: improve cross-region fallback latency, surface quota headroom metric to ops.

RAW METRIC SNAPSHOT (representative for CASE1 run, us-west1 2026-06-03 14:00->18:00 UTC):
Time	Active GPUs	Queued reqs	Per-GPU util	Probe-failures/s	Scale-events
14:00	48	12	0.67	0	0
14:30	46	18	0.72	1	1 scale-down
15:10	44	25	0.80	3 (jitter burst)	2 scale-downs
16:05	50	6	0.55	0	1 scale-up
17:40	48	10	0.60	2	0

OBSERVATIONS & INTERPRETATIONS:
- Probe-failure handling is the single largest source of spurious scale-downs in noisy networks. Simple fix (probe-squelch 2 consecutive) reduced false-downs by ~78% in pilot.
- Aggressive scale-up parameters reduce SLA violations but materially increase token cost; need region-specific cost thresholds.
- Telemetry lag creates false positives for scale-up when metrics arrive late; prefer conservative growth with max burst buffer.
- Regional quota ceilings are an operational dependency: autoscaler must be quota-aware and escalate to cross-region fallback sooner.

ACTION ITEMS (owners + due dates):
- Implement probe-squelch and adjustable probe-timeout per-region (Owner: Marcus Li) Due: 2026-06-12
- Add 'pre-warm' annotation to routes for scheduled/suspected traffic spikes (Owner: Rebecca Owens) Due: 2026-06-15
- Implement weighted-decay window in metric aggregator to reduce impact of delayed spikes (Owner: Samir Patel) Due: 2026-06-20
- Create regional quota-monitor and early fallback hook (Owner: Tania Rios) Due: 2026-06-22
- Run 72h regression test across all regions with updated policy flags (Owner: Elena Garcia) Due: 2026-07-01

RISK & ROLLBACK PLAN:
- Risk: probe-squelch may delay legitimate scale-downs, increasing steady-state cost. Rollback: revert probe-squelch flag for region and enable cost watch alert. Any rollback must be a coordinated change with on-call and product.

NOTES FOR SRE ON-CALL:
- If seeing repeated scale-downs correlated with high probe-failure counts, toggle 'probe-squelch' beta flag for the region and monitor p95.
- If scale-up latency exceeds 180s repeatedly, open JIRA-ENGINF-762 and escalate to infra-boot team.

APPENDIX (quick commands and dashboards):
- Query candidate logs: logs:prod.autoscaler "probe_failure" region=us-west1 | summarize count() by 1m
- Dashboards: Autoscale -> Region -> ProbeFailures / ScaleEvents (bookmark id: confluence:Autoscale-Playbook-v2#dash-3)
- Simulation harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/tree/main/sim/harness (use config: chaos-testplan-2026.yaml)

LAST NOTES:
This sheet is intentionally pragmatic and iteration-focused. The goal is to find brittle interactions (probe timing, telemetry lag, quota ceilings) and produce small, measurable mitigations that can be turned on region-by-region. Keep entries concise; add experiment rows as we discover new failure modes.
